title: Can You Finish All Courses
statement:
A school offers `n` courses numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Some courses have **prerequisites**: each entry `prerequisites[i] = [a, b]` means you must finish course `b` **before** you can take course `a`.

Return `true` if it is possible to finish **all** the courses, otherwise `false` (which happens when the prerequisites contain a circle, like course 0 needing 1 and course 1 needing 0).
constraints: each pair [a, b] has a != b and 0 <= a, b < n (a pair may repeat)

examples.explanation: Each course needs the other first.

hints.nudge: Which courses can you take right away? What changes after you take one?
hints.pattern: Topological sort (Kahn's algorithm): repeatedly take a course whose prerequisites are all done.
hints.pseudocode:
indegree[a] = number of prerequisites of a; adj[b] = courses that need b
queue = courses with indegree 0; taken = 0
while queue: c = pop; taken++; for each course x needing c: indegree[x]--; if 0: push x
return taken == n
hints.walkthrough: Count, for every course, how many unfinished prerequisites it has. Courses with zero can be taken now: put them in a queue. Taking a course finishes a prerequisite for every course that needs it, so reduce their counts, and queue any that reach zero. If you manage to take all n courses, there is no circle. If some courses never reach zero, they are stuck waiting on each other in a cycle, so the answer is false. O(n + m) time.
